I can't even congratulate my friend genuinely because I'm too busy choking on my own envy and feeling like a complete failure.

I hate myself for being this jealous, but why does it have to be so easy for them while I have to bleed for a passing grade?

I muted the group immediately because my heart started racing and I felt like I was going to throw up. I haven't even cleared my system design round yet, my CGPA is a 5.8, and I’m terrified that if I go back home for the holidays, everyone will look at me with pity. My roommate just uploaded a reel of her weekend trip to a fancy cafe with her new office friends. She got placed in a fintech firm last month, and her life looks so aesthetic and perfect now. Meanwhile, I'm literally eating cold maggi in our messy room, staring at my Excel sheet trying to prepare for another gruelling mock viva tomorrow. I feel so ugly, left behind, and desperately lonely.

I can't even open Snapchat anymore without getting a panic attack. Everyone from my high school is posting pictures from their high-paying tech jobs, getting married, or moving abroad. I had to take a drop year because of my severe depression, my prep for GATE is going horribly, and I feel like I'm frozen in time while the world is running at 100 mph. How do I stop comparing my absolute rock bottom with their peak moments?

Just opened LinkedIn and literally every second post is 'I'm thrilled to share I accepted an offer at Google/Microsoft'. Meanwhile, I got rejected in the first round of a mass recruiter yesterday because I choked on a basic DP problem in the coding lab. My dad sent me a screenshot of some relative's son's post about landing a 25 LPA package, asking me what I'm doing with my life. I've got two backlogs in my 5th sem and my CGPA is a literal joke. I feel sick to my stomach looking at these posts, like my entire future is already over before it even started.

I had to mute my entire WhatsApp group chat today. Everyone is posting pictures from their weekend trips, expensive cafes, or celebrating their first paychecks, while I'm stuck in this tiny PG room eating cold maggi and grinding for GATE for the second time. I saw my lab partner's Insta story at a concert and I just broke down crying. I'm sacrifice-burnout exhausted, but what hurts more is this disgusting envy eating me up inside because I want what they have so bad. I feel like a bitter, miserable loser who's just wasting their youth on mock tests.

I can't escape it. On X it's 'build in public' and 19-year-olds making 5k USD a month, and on LinkedIn it's classmates posting about their Summer Internships. I can barely solve 2 Leetcode easy questions without looking at the solutions, and my DSA lab exam is next week. It's like everyone received some secret manual on how to succeed and I'm the only one who missed it. I just stare at my VS Code screen feeling completely paralyzed, wishing I could delete my internet presence and disappear.

My mom just forwarded a post in the family WhatsApp group about my cousin getting a massive promotion in London. She didn't say anything to me, but the silence is louder than any scolding. I'm currently struggling to even clear my CGPA cutoff of 6.5, and I have three pending assignments due by midnight. I feel so much shame looking at how happy everyone is on social media while I'm just this heavy burden on my parents' finances. I hate this constant, public scorecard of our lives.

I got rejected from the college coding club yesterday after three grueling rounds of interviews. Today, my feed is flooded with 'super excited to join the core team' posts from classmates who I know copied half their assignments in the first semester. I feel this incredibly toxic mix of anger and self-pity. Why does everyone else get the opportunities, the networking, and the clean resumes while I'm left on the outside looking in? I feel so invisible and worthless.

Logged into LinkedIn today and literally felt a physical punch in my stomach. This guy from my batch who barely cleared his backlogs in 2nd year just posted a picture holding a mock check of 42 LPA. Meanwhile, I'm sitting here with my 6.2 CGPA, staring at a red screen on Leetcode because my binary search tree is throwing a segmentation fault. My dad called an hour ago asking if I heard about Sharmaji's son getting into Microsoft. I can't breathe. I feel like such a massive, pathetic failure.

Everyone is on Instagram posting these aesthetic reels of their weekend trips to Gokarna or celebrating their early PPO parties with their 'tech squads'. I spent my entire Sunday locked in this stuffy hostel room trying to debug a Django project that won't even compile, feeling like my life is passing me by. I can't even open my WhatsApp without seeing people share their offer letters in the batch group chat. It genuinely makes me feel so bitter and angry, and then I hate myself even more for being so toxic.

My aunt just spammed our family WhatsApp group with pictures of my cousin getting his visa stamped for his MS in Germany, and my mom just sighed and walked out of the room. I have two backlogs in civil engineering and can't even clear the first round of campus placements because my aptitude test scores are garbage. Every time I see these updates on my feed, it's like a constant reminder that I'm the disappointment of the family. I just want to delete my accounts and disappear, I'm so tired of pretending I'm okay.

I can't even scroll through LinkedIn anymore without getting a panic attack. My lab partner just got a summer internship at Goldman Sachs and posted this long, cheesy 'humbled and honored' post that got 500 likes. My dad took out a massive loan for my coaching and engineering fees, and here I am, still getting rejected in the resume screening rounds of basic startups. Seeing her success doesn't inspire me; it just fills me with this absolute dread that I've wasted my parents' hard-earned money.

Everyone on my Twitter feed is 'building in public', launching SaaS products, and sharing GitHub green graphs like they don't even sleep. Meanwhile, my executive dysfunction is so bad I've been staring at the same VS Code terminal for three days, unable to even write a basic API endpoint for my final year project. I feel so pathetic and useless compared to these 19-year-old geniuses who seem to have life entirely figured out. It feels like I'm already obsolete before my career has even started.

I literally can't open LinkedIn anymore. Every single scroll is just 'I'm incredibly humbled to announce...' with some insane package at a FAANG company. Here I am, stuck on a basic recursion lab for my DSA backlog, with my dad constantly sending me screenshots of my cousin's placement offer in our family group chat. It feels like everyone got the manual on how to succeed and I was just left behind in the dirt.

My high school group chat is basically dead because they all made new, cooler friends at Tier-1 NITs. I'm sitting here in my tiny hostel room studying for a 7:30 AM class tomorrow, watching their Instagram stories of weekend road trips and campus fests. It makes me feel so pathetic, like my entire life is just one massive, boring chore while they got the actual 'college experience' I worked so hard for.

I saw Rahul's post about landing the off-campus SDE role at Microsoft. We literally sat next to each other in the web dev labs and I was the one who explained APIs to him last semester. I couldn't even pass the initial resume screening, and seeing his post with 500+ likes and my professors commenting 'so proud of you' makes me feel this sick, toxic knot in my chest. I want to be happy for him, but honestly, it just makes me want to disappear.

My entire WhatsApp feed is flooded with screenshots of CAT scorecards today. People I used to help with prep are posting '99.5 percentile!' and sharing their IIM shortlist emails. I missed the sectional cutoff by 0.5 marks and my mom is in the other room talking on the phone with my aunt, comparing our scores. I've muted everyone's status but the shame is still screaming in my head every time I look at my phone.

I can't escape the 'build in public' tech Twitter crowd. Every 20-year-old is apparently a founder, raising pre-seed funding, or making $5k/month on side projects while I'm struggling to get out of bed for a compiler design class. I feel like an absolute NPC, just watching other people play life on creative mode while I'm drowning in routine midterms and coding assignments that don't even matter.

Placements season is on and LinkedIn is absolutely flooded with those 'I am thrilled to share...' posts. A classmate who literally copied his way through our DSA coding labs just posted about bagging a 45 LPA offer package at a FAANG. I am sitting here with 2 active backlogs, struggling to even optimize a simple graph algorithm for a mock test, feeling like an absolute zero. Instagram is even worse—everyone is out celebrating at premium cafes while I eat cold hostel food and stare at my blank IDE. Why does it feel like everyone got the cheat codes to life while I am stuck in this pit?

My Instagram feed is literally killing me slowly. Every single person from my coaching institute batch is posting stories of their elite college fests, trips to Goa, or getting into cool campus clubs. Meanwhile, I am stuck in this tiny, damp PG room, preparing for a partial drop, scoring miserable marks in my online mock tests. I deactivated my account twice but I keep logging back in from Chrome just to torture myself and see how far behind I've fallen. I feel so pathetic for being this obsessed with their lives while mine is in ruins.

My cousin just posted on our extended WhatsApp family group about getting a 12 LPA entry-level systems analyst job. Immediately, my dad forwarded the screenshot to me with a passive-aggressive 'Congratulations to him, hope you are studying' text. I have my midterms next week and my CGPA is sitting at a literal 6.4. I spent the last three hours doomscrolling LinkedIn, looking at other analyst profiles and feeling this sickening dread in my chest that I will never get a package like that and I will forever remain the disappointment of the family.

Every time I open LinkedIn, someone from my department is sharing certificates of 3 different summer internships or open-source contributions. I can barely manage to wake up and attend my 9 AM lectures because of my severe depression. I feel so incredibly lazy and defective looking at their hyper-productivity. How is everyone doing so much while I'm struggling to just wash my clothes, eat a proper meal, and not cry in my room?

I accidentally saw my ex's LinkedIn update today—she got into an Ivy League university for her Masters. I wanted to pursue that dream too, but my family's financial situation crashed during COVID and I had to take a low-paying local service-based IT job to pay off my sibling's tuition fees. Looking at her happy pictures outside a foreign campus makes me feel so bitter and angry at my own life. I feel like a failure who is destined to stay stuck in this middle-class rut forever while everyone else flies away to live their dreams.

I just opened LinkedIn and saw my lab partner posted about getting a 45 LPA SDE internship at a FAANG company. I'm literally sitting in my hostel room with 3 backlogs, trying to debug a basic binary tree in C++, and crying because my CGPA is a 6.2. Why does everyone have their life sorted out while I can't even get a local startup to view my resume?

Every time I check Instagram, someone from my batch is posting about their weekend trips to Goa or their fancy cafes, while I'm stuck grinding in this coaching center library for 14 hours a day with nothing to show for it but a terrible mock test score. My parents keep asking me when I'll get a real package like my cousin. I feel like such a failure, staring at these perfect lives through a screen while mine is just slipping away.

The college WhatsApp group is blowing up because the placement committee just shared the list of selected students for the high-paying fintech roles. I didn't even clear the first round of coding, and seeing my friends post 'congratulations' stickers to each other makes my stomach turn with actual physical sickness. I want to be happy for them, but honestly, I just feel this deep, toxic resentment and shame that I am the one left behind.

My roommate just uploaded a vlog of her weekend with her friends, looking so pretty and happy, and I'm sitting here with greasy hair, eating instant noodles, crying over my DSA assignment. Her life looks like a movie and mine feels like a punishment. I hate how much I envy her, and I hate myself even more for being this bitter when she is actually nice to me.

Everyone on LinkedIn is posting their 'excited to announce' updates about securing summer research internships abroad. I applied to thirty places, spent nights emailing professors, got rejected by all, and now my feed is just a wall of my classmates' success. I feel so invisible, like my hard work means absolutely nothing to anyone and I am just destined to be a nobody.

I swear to god, opening LinkedIn or Instagram is like self-harm at this point. Everyone in my batch is posting these blue 'I’m happy to share...' updates about their summer internships at FAANG, or photos from some fancy cafe in Bangalore. My CGPA is stuck at 6.8 and I just feel like a complete waste of space. Why does everyone else have their life sorted out while I can't even get my code to compile without getting a headache?

My family WhatsApp group is a nightmare. Today my uncle posted a screenshot of my cousin’s Instagram story about getting a 18 LPA package at some fintech startup, and my dad immediately messaged me asking how my placement prep is going. I didn't even get shortlisted for the second round of campus interviews yesterday because I choked during the system design viva. I spent the last three hours scrolling through my batchmates' LinkedIn profiles, watching them celebrate their offers while I literally feel like throwing up from anxiety. I feel like such a disappointment to my parents.

It honestly feels like there's some secret handbook on 'how to succeed' that everyone else got at birth, and I was just left behind in the dark. I feel so isolated, like I'm the only one in my whole college who is genuinely drowning.

I had to mute my class Discord server today. Everyone is discussing their Kaggle rankings, their open-source contributions, and how they finished the entire web-dev project over the weekend. I spent my weekend crying over my failing midterm grades and trying to summon the energy to just wash my clothes. Seeing their constant productivity porn makes me feel so inadequate, like I don’t even deserve to be in this branch. I feel like a fraud who somehow sneaked into this college and is now about to get exposed.
